result.title: LatentQuant: Preserving the Policy-Facing Latent Contract under NVFP4 VAE Quantization
result.summary: Recent world action models (WAMs) reuse pretrained video VAEs whose encoder latents directly condition downstream action policies. Quantization must therefore preserve not only reconstruction fidelity but also the policy-facing latent contract expected by the frozen policy. Direct NVFP4 leaves W4A4 quantization error uncompensated, whereas joint quantization-aware training (QAT) can recover reconstruction by moving this representation. On Wan2.1, joint QAT nearly matches FP32 VBench-7 (0.7403 versus 0.7409), yet LIBERO success collapses from 95.5% to 10.5%. Controlled decoder-only experiments show that activation quantize-dequantize operations alter the reconstruction signal and decoder Jacobian, redirecting the gradient returned to the encoder and inducing persistent latent drift. Based on this mechanism, we introduce LatentQuant, a two-stage NVFP4 QAT framework that first aligns the quantized encoder with its high-precision counterpart, then freezes it while adapting the decoder. Across Wan2.1 and Wan2.2, LatentQuant preserves near-baseline control and high reconstruction quality, achieving 95.75% success on LIBERO and 68.8% on RoboTwin. On NVIDIA B300 GPUs, NVFP4 execution achieves 1.17x-1.26x end-to-end VAE speedups over BF16 cuDNN.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作研究视频 VAE 在 NVFP4 量化下的潜变量漂移问题，发现联合 QAT 虽保持重建质量却使下游策略成功率崩塌，并提出两阶段量化框架以对齐量化编码器与高精度编码器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜在表示承载下游契约、量化扰动导致梯度回流与持续潜变量漂移」的机制，可能与 LVR 中视觉旁路、信息坍缩及 latent 内容是否被下游真正使用的问题形成类比线索，可供核查但领域偏离较远。
